claims.quote: Loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene underlie the familial cancer syndrome neurofibromatosis type I (NF1).
Loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene underlie the familial cancer syndrome neurofibromatosis type I (NF1).
The NF1-encoded protein, neurofibromin, functions as a Ras-GTPase activating protein (RasGAP).
Accordingly, deregulation of Ras is thought to contribute to NF1 development.
We show here that the mTOR pathway is tightly regulated by neurofibromin.
The NF1 tumor suppressor critically regulates TSC2 and mTOR.

Furthermore, while we show that the activation of endogenous Ras leads to constitutive mTOR signaling in this disease state, we also demonstrate that in normal cells Ras is differentially required for mTOR signaling in response to various growth factors.

Importantly, tumor cell lines derived from NF1 patients, and a genetically engineered cell system that requires Nf1-deficiency for transformation, are highly sensitive to the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin.
